A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BalSAM study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across pagination and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original tree-crown segmentation experiments on Quebec Plantations, SBL and BCI, including three-seed benchmark results and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Mask2Former comparisons, DSM-only and focal-loss experiments, and inference-speed measurements.

M1.justification: BalSAM's DSM encoder, element-wise embedding fusion, SAM decoder integration and architectural variants remain unchanged (Figures 2 and 10). The added model and loss configurations expand baseline and ablation experiments without revising the proposed BalSAM procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same tree-crown tasks, forest domains and taxonomic groupings on Quebec Plantations, SBL and BCI. New experiments reuse this coverage; COCO is introduced as the source of pretrained weights, not an additional dataset evaluated by this study.

E2.justification: v2 adds a substantive non-SAM transformer comparison family: Mask2Former with Swin-base and Swin-L backbones, each evaluated with RGB and RGB+DSM on Quebec Plantations (Table 1). Existing comparators remain, and the SBL loss comparison additionally includes focal loss.

E3.justification: Appendix B.6 changes the reported Mask R-CNN epoch limits from 100/200/300 to 100/300/500 for Plantations/SBL/BCI; the PDFs do not establish reruns. New experiments introduce Mask2Former configurations with 384×384 inputs, modality/loss controls and timing on a common V100 GPU. Existing splits and accuracy metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds targeted analyses of DSM informativeness using DSM-only Mask R-CNN on Plantations and SBL (Appendix D.1), focal loss with gamma 2 for class imbalance, and inference efficiency. Existing prompt/score, DSM-integration, post-processing and BalSAM-variant analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The existing three-seed averages, standard errors in result tables and standard deviations in Figure 11 remain unchanged. Added Mask2Former and focal-loss rows follow the existing error-reporting convention. No new statistical procedure or changed run count is documented; the new DSM-only table does not specify uncertainty.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are retained, but substantial new evidence is reported. Table 1 adds Mask2Former RGB/RGB+DSM wmAP values of 42.24/47.15 for Swin-base and 52.92/51.72 for Swin-L. New results also include DSM-only mIoU of 0.734/0.289 on Plantations/SBL (Table 14), focal-loss wmAP of 23.49 on SBL (Table 17), and inference timings and parameter counts (Table 10).

T1.justification: The metric definitions and hierarchical-loss construction are retained, with the latter moving from Appendix D.3.1 to D.4.1. Neither version provides theoretical results or proofs, and v2 introduces no new derivation or formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions retain the same scientific scope: benchmarking tree-crown segmentation, introducing BalSAM, finding limitations of out-of-the-box SAM, and identifying forest-dependent benefits from DSM information. Additional evidence and future directions do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: New Section 5.3 gives practical model-selection guidance and questions the feasibility of individual-tree carbon mapping in tropical forests. Appendix B.2 adds limitations concerning terrain elevation and transferring DSM thresholds between sites. The conclusion expands future directions, while existing canopy-complexity and class-imbalance interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v1 supplies sample code and promises a later full release; v2 identifies a public project repository and reports preprocessing/training code availability, although checklist item 13 retains future-release wording. v2 also documents site-to-split assignments and nonoverlap (Table 7), prompt-processing details, and new baseline and timing configurations.

R1.justification: v2 adds references 64–69 covering Mask2Former, COCO, OAM-TCD, tropical species mapping, large-tree carbon importance and Sat-SINR. These support the added comparisons and application discussion; the related-work section and central novelty positioning remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most scientific prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 adds a Recommendations subsection, expands selected explanations and the conclusion, revises author and acknowledgment text, separates the funding statement, and appends a NeurIPS checklist.

P2.justification: v2 adds tables for site assignments, efficiency and DSM-only results, and expands the benchmark and loss tables. Existing figures are retained with resizing or relocation, while table uncertainty typography and the author-block layout are compacted. The overall visual organization remains recognizable.

improvement.justification: The added transformer comparisons, direct DSM-only control, efficiency measurements and clearer split/access documentation modestly strengthen the evidence and practical usefulness. Gains are limited by Mask2Former's different input resolution and the new blanket DSM-benefit statement despite declining Swin-L scores in Table 1. DSM-only results also lack uncertainty reporting. The core findings remain unchanged.
